seoTitle: How to Add Domains to the Allowlist in Google Workspace
metaDescription: Step-by-step guide to adding trusted domains to your Google Workspace allowlist so their emails reach your inbox securely in 2026.
intro: An allowlist tells Google Workspace which domains should always be trusted, helping legitimate emails avoid being flagged or filtered as spam. This guide shows admins how to add domains to the allowlist correctly.

steps.heading: Access the Admin Console
steps.body: Sign in with an admin account and head to the Apps section, where Gmail's email safety settings are managed.

steps.heading: Find the allowlist settings
steps.body: Navigate to the compliance or spam settings area where you can define trusted senders and domains.

steps.heading: Add the domain to your allowlist
steps.body: Enter the domain you want to trust so mail from it bypasses standard spam filtering rules.

steps.heading: Verify the domain was added
steps.body: Check the list after saving to confirm the domain appears correctly and test by sending a message from that domain.

steps.heading: Review the allowlist periodically
steps.body: Revisit your allowlist occasionally to remove domains you no longer need to trust, keeping your organization's email security tight.

faq.question: Why would I need to allowlist a domain in Google Workspace?
faq.answer: Allowlisting is useful when legitimate emails from a trusted partner, vendor, or internal tool keep getting caught in spam filters.

faq.question: Does allowlisting a domain apply to all users in my organization?
faq.answer: Yes, admin-level allowlist changes typically apply organization-wide rather than to a single user's inbox.

faq.question: Is allowlisting the same as whitelisting an IP address?
faq.answer: They're related but different — domain allowlisting trusts a sender's domain, while IP whitelisting trusts a specific sending server.

faq.question: Can allowlisting a domain create a security risk?
faq.answer: Yes, if misused it can let spoofed emails through, so only allowlist domains you're confident are legitimate and trusted.
